summary: Sawtooth National Forest lookout built 1922, staffed by husband-and-wife teams in the 1930s, rebuilt in 1961, now a remote emergency lookout reached by trail.

facts.status_note: Described as kept available for emergency use rather than regularly staffed or rented.

access.note: Reached only by trail (foot, horseback, or motorcycle); no public rental found.

visit.trail_note: About a 12-air-mile trip southeast of Featherville; a roughly 5-hour horse pack along the telephone line trail per a 1986 newspaper account.

facts.agency: US Forest Service - Sawtooth National Forest

events.note: Cabin built atop Iron Mountain, a California Region 5 Plan 4A design.
Mr. and Mrs. Neil Platts stationed at the lookout for the season.
Niel Platt staffed the lookout for the fire season.
Mr. and Mrs. Clair Pond finished a season staffing the lookout.
Current two-story R-6 flat-top cab on an enclosed tower built, replacing the 1922 cabin.
Forest Service sought a volunteer to staff the tower for the season; access described as by trail only, with helicopter transport offered.
Added to the National Historic Lookout Register, September 30, 2020.

evidence.quote:
A lookout cabin was built atop Iron Mountain in 1922, a California Region 5 Plan 4A design.
The structure was replaced in 1961 with the current R-6 Flat Top on an enclosed tower.

evidence.supports: 1922 cabin and 1961 two-story R-6 flat cab
R-5 ground cab circa 1921 and 1961 replacement kept for emergencies
evidence.quote: Preceeded by a R-5 ground cab built in 1921, the present 2-story R-6 flat cab, built in 1961, is available for emergencies.
Mr. and Mrs. Neil Platts are stationed at the Iron Mountain lookout for the season. Platts reports 21 as the lowest relative humidity reading recorded this year.
Mr. and Mrs. Clair Pond, who have had charge of Iron Mountain lookout on Soldier mountain this past season, have finished their work there and moved back to the Prairie Wednesday.

evidence.supports: 1986 volunteer call and trail access description
evidence.quote: Jack Exon, fire management officer for the Fairfield Ranger District of the Sawtooth National Forest, is looking for someone who would like to volunteer their time this summer to man the district's Iron Mountain fire lookout tower.

evidence.supports: access by trail, 12 air miles, helicopter transport offered
evidence.quote: The lookout sits on top of the 9,694-foot Iron Mountain, approximately 12 air miles southeast of Featherville, Access to the lookout is by trail, through the use of motorcycles, foot, or horseback.

evidence.supports: trail follows telephone line, about 5-hour horse pack
evidence.quote: TRAIL FOLLOWS THE TELEPHONE LINE. ABOUT A 5-HOUR HORSE PACK.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR and Idaho Fire Lookouts date the first structure to 1922; firelookout.com says 1921. Both describe the same early R-5/Plan 4A ground cabin, so this is likely a one-year discrepancy in the same build rather than two different structures.

notes_for_editor: idahofirelookouts.com has no documented staffing history for this lookout; the Weebly site supplied strong newspaper-sourced staffing detail instead. No current rental or regular staffing was found; status_note reflects firelookout.com's 'available for emergencies' description, which may be dated.
